title: Reaching the complete graph by closure steps forces a Hamiltonian cycle
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $\nu \ge 3$ vertices. Suppose the complete graph on the vertices of $G$ can be obtained from $G$ by finitely many (possibly zero) Bondy--Chv\'atal closure steps, each of which joins some pair of distinct nonadjacent vertices whose degrees sum to at least $\nu$. Then $G$ is Hamiltonian, that is, $G$ has a cycle through all of its vertices.
hypotheses_covered: the complete graph is reachable from $G$ by the reflexive-transitive closure of the closure-step relation (finitely many, possibly zero, closure steps)
each step: distinct nonadjacent pair with degree sum at least $\nu$
